F2 IS THE RESULT, AND IT FAILED. Permuting labels WITHIN complex leaves the refitted
model at 0.5742, not 0.5. That null was built to catch exactly one thing and it
caught it: a within-complex permutation preserves each complex's BREAKER COUNT, so any
feature that is large in complexes with many breakers keeps its association. Contact
count is such a feature -- big interfaces have both -- so roughly 0.57 of every
POOLED number on this task is complex identity rather than variant discrimination.
THAT FLOOR APPLIES TO EVERY POOLED NUMBER HERE, NOT ONLY TO THIS ONE: the 0.7765
contact count of loop 52, nexus's recorded 0.755 and rebuilt 0.770, and this
model's 0.7736 all sit on top of it. The comparison that does not is F5's, which is
paired WITHIN complex -- and there the fitted physics adds +0.0180 over geometry,
winning 51.6% of complexes at p 0.042. Real, and small.
Weighting the terms took energy alone from 0.6268 to 0.5992 and the full model
to 0.7736 held out by complex, with a train-test gap of +0.0141.
THE ENERGY STILL DOES NOT BEAT THE TAPE MEASURE ON ITS OWN (0.5992 vs 0.7765), which
is the third time counting has won here. What F5 asks separately is whether it adds
anything on top, and that answer is yes.
The parameter-free claim of loop 52 is GONE and is not being smuggled back: these weights
were fitted, F1 prints the train-test gap, and F2 refits the entire pipeline under 200 within-complex
label permutations to show what the fitting could have manufactured.
